name: Kingdom of Prussia

areaKm2.note: world_1800 "Prussia" polygons = 287,200 + 41,000 km2 (eastern block and Westphalian lands) on the sphere.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1816 = 10,349k for post-1815 Prussia. Pre-Tilsit Prussia (with South and New East Prussia, Ansbach, Westphalian lands) ~9.7-10.7M; Tilsit roughly halved it.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) Germany 1800 = 12.5%, Poland 1800 = 4.8%; Prussia with its Polish provinces ~10%.

activePersonnel.note: Page infobox: Prussia 254,000 engaged (Clodfelter 2017 p. 150). Peacetime establishment ~240,000 incl. ~1/3 foreign enlisted men and cantonists on furlough 10 months a year; lower bound allows for paper strength.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: no Landwehr before 1813; only depot and invalid companies and the Saxon ally (18,000, excluded).

supportPersonnel.note: Four foot artillery regiments and horse artillery ~13,000, pontonniers, train and staff. No navy. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: Prussia mobilised ~280,000 from ~4.9M in 1813 (5.7%) under an emergency Landwehr system the 1806 state lacked.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 58-60 line regiments of 2 musketeer battalions plus grenadier battalions at ~600-700 present.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: M1782 musket, one of the worst of the era

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: superb parade-ground drill in obsolete linear tactics

count.note: 24 fusilier battalions and the Feldjaeger regiment.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: jaeger rifles

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: too few light troops for the French skirmish swarm

count.note: 13 cuirassier regiments (incl. Gens d'armes, Garde du Corps).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: big horses, no cuirass worn in 1806

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Frederician cavalry tradition

count.note: 14 dragoon and 10 hussar regiments plus Towarczys.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: good horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: well drilled, poorly used for reconnaissance

count.note: Educated guess: field and battalion guns of the field army; the War of the Fourth Coalition page says over 4,000 artillery pieces were lost in all, mostly fortress guns.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: heavy obsolescent pieces, battalion guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: guns dispersed, horse teams hired

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: aged Brunswick and Hohenlohe, divided councils, Jena-Auerstedt on 14 October

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: a third foreign mercenaries, harsh discipline; collapsed after Jena, but some fortresses held (Kolberg)

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Frederician prestige and overconfidence

weapons.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: M1782 musket below the anchor; heavy field artillery

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: cuirassiers without cuirass

ships.note: Anchor: 6 (74-gun ships of the line). Evidence: Prussia had no navy in 1806; level reflects Baltic merchant shipbuilding at Stettin and Danzig

fortification.note: Anchor: 6 (Vauban-type forts). Evidence: Magdeburg, Kuestrin, Stettin, Kolberg, Danzig, Graudenz

logistics.note: Anchor: 6 (magazines + requisition). Evidence: tents and magazine trains made the army slow (van Creveld ch. 2)

communications.note: Anchor: 6 (semaphore telegraph). Evidence: no optical telegraph until 1832

isr.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: lost track of Napoleon's advance through the Thuringian Forest

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID) Germany 1805 = 1,725; Poland 1800 = 902. Prussia with its Polish provinces ~1,500.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: the army took about two-thirds of Prussian state spending; mobilised from August 1806.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Silesian linen and mining, Berlin manufactures.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: grain exporter via Danzig and Koenigsberg.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field-gun output of the Berlin foundry per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Prussia had few paved chaussees in 1806 (~2,000 km), mostly unpaved post roads.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Koenigsberg, Danzig, Stettin, Kolberg, Memel, Emden.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Baltic grain and timber fleet.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row: familiar terrain and fortresses; open North German plain, population support passive.

notes: Snapshot = Kingdom of Prussia in early October 1806, before Jena-Auerstedt. Territory and population = pre-Tilsit Prussia incl. the Polish partition provinces (South Prussia with Warsaw, New East Prussia) and the western enclaves; includes is empty (Saxony, an ally with 18,000 men, is excluded). Personnel: the whole standing army = active (cantonists on furlough counted, as they were on the establishment); no Landwehr existed. Page figures: Prussia 254,000 (Clodfelter via the War of the Fourth Coalition page); casualties 40,000+ and 165,000 captured. Branch split, artillery and the 1806 population are reconstructions (grade C/D).
